minutes.headline: Board of Health unanimously approved a tight tank, well variances, and two septic upgrades, all by roll call.
minutes.summary: A remote Board of Health meeting heard four septic and well requests: 25 Pearl Street, 474 West Street and 189 Hemlock Drive. All were approved by roll call, with conditions on the tight tank. The agent gave a COVID-19 and flu clinic update, and a former member spoke about the TCP commercial kitchen.

public_comment.topic: Owner of 189 Hemlock Drive asked where and when to pick up the permit he needs to close on the house.
A former board member listened in, thanked the board, and said the TCP commercial kitchen may need a board discussion.
public_comment.stated_role: former board member and member of the TCP redesign committee

votes.motion: Approve the 4,000 gallon tight tank at 25 Pearl Street, designed for two bedrooms, with a deed notation, plus regular pumping and maintenance.
Approve the two well regulation variances at 25 Pearl Street to allow a well pit below grade in the driveway.
votes.outcome: passed by roll call; no dissent heard

votes.motion: Grant a local upgrade at 474 West Street reducing separation to groundwater from four feet to three feet.
Approve the variances for the septic repair at 189 Hemlock Drive.

decisions.decision: Board asked for a deed notation of the tight tank and its two-bedroom limit, and a first-year operation and maintenance contract.
The tight tank is to be pumped about monthly at first, with pumping receipts reported, to measure actual flow.
Board may invite the agent to a TCP committee meeting about the commercial kitchen.

what_happened.line: The Board of Health approved a tight tank at 25 Pearl Street by unanimous roll call, with a deed notation limiting it to two bedrooms and regular pumping.
The board approved two well regulation variances at 25 Pearl Street, allowing a well pit below grade in the driveway; no dissent was heard.
The board granted a local upgrade at 474 West Street reducing separation to groundwater, by unanimous roll call.
The board approved variances for the septic repair at 189 Hemlock Drive, unanimously.
The tight tank is to be pumped about monthly at first, with receipts reported to measure actual flow.

why_it_matters: The tight tank conditions (deed notation, bedroom limit, monthly pumping at first, receipts) show what a property owner takes on with a holding tank, including ongoing pumping costs and a limit on future use of the house.
Septic and well variances decide whether a home can be repaired or sold, as the Hemlock Drive owner's need for a permit to close on the house shows.
